source_locator.edition_or_translation: J. M. Ashmand translation from Proclus's Greek paraphrase; 1900 W. Foulsham & Co. new edition
source_locator.section: Faces, Chariots, and Other Similar Attributes of the Planets
source_locator.short_quote: when a planet occupies a place adverse and dissimilar in condition to itself, much of its influence is dissipated and lost

calculation_dependencies: comparison of the occupied sign's condition with the planet's condition

condition.occupied_sign_condition: adverse and dissimilar to the planet
condition.source_consequence: much influence is dissipated and lost

normalized_rule: When a planet occupies a sign adverse and dissimilar to its own condition, classify much of its influence as dissipated and lost.
synthesis_notes: This is a traditional astrological influence rule, not a psychological or scientific claim about a person's behavior.
review_notes: Keep this adverse/dissimilar-sign condition separate from generic maltreatment, proper face, and rejoicing; the source describes a sign-condition interaction.
transmission_notes: The consequence is stated in the Ashmand/Proclus main text. The rule preserves the source's influence language and does not import later maltreatment terminology.
